*   **Time Complexity:** $O(1)$ per light source per fragment.
The cost is dominated by a few dot products, a power function, and vector arithmetic.
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(1)$ for material and light parameters.
*   **When to use:** Real-time applications where performance is critical and physical accuracy is not required.
Good for stylized rendering or as a baseline lighting model.
*   **When not to use:** Physically based rendering (PBR) pipelines, scenes requiring accurate energy conservation, or when realistic shadowing and global illumination are needed.
It was introduced as an empirical model to approximate the way light reflects off surfaces, specifically focusing on the specular highlight.
It became a standard in computer graphics due to its simplicity and visual effectiveness.
